newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France confirms EU summit on May 23.
newsitem.headline: France confirms EU summit on May 23.

text.p: French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier said on Tuesday that the European Union would hold a special summit next month to speed up its negotiations on a new treaty.
"There will be a meeting of the heads of state and government on May 23," Barnier told reporters.

Talks on a new treaty are due to be wrapped up at the EU's mid-year summit in Amsterdam in June. But little agreement has been reached to date, in part because the bloc is waiting for Britain's elections on May 1.
Britain's ruling Conservative government is opposed to many of the proposals being negotiated, but is widely expected to be defeated by the opposition Labour party.
A summit on May 23 would be Labour leader Tony Blair's first chance to show how his government differs on Europe from the Conservatives if he is elected..
Officals said last week that a summit was likely on May 23, but it had not been confirmed.
Barnier did not say where the summiot would be held. Officials have suggested it may take place on the Dutch town of Maastricht, whether the EU's last treaty was agreed in 1991.
